macro_markets.query: What are the most important macroeconomic and stock market news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include major index movements, Fed/central bank news, and significant company earnings or announcements.

items.title: U.S. stocks close higher as yields stay elevated
items.summary: Major U.S. indexes finished the session higher, with the S&P 500 up 0.51%, the Dow up 0.93%, and the Nasdaq up 0.48%. The move came despite ongoing pressure from rising Treasury yields and a bond-market selloff.

items.title: 30-year Treasury yield climbs to highest level since 2004
items.summary: The U.S. 30-year Treasury yield rose to 5.53%, its highest since June 2004, underscoring a sharp selloff in longer-dated government bonds. Reuters-linked market coverage also noted the longer-dated yield run-up after upbeat economic data.

items.title: Mortgage rates top 7% again as bond yields rise
items.summary: The average 30-year fixed mortgage rate rose to 7.03%, the highest since January 2025, according to Freddie Mac. The increase adds to affordability pressure in the U.S. housing market.

items.title: Jobless claims fall to 197,000, keeping labor market firm
items.summary: Initial U.S. unemployment claims fell to 197,000, the lowest since mid-July, while the four-week average also declined. The data reinforced the view that labor-market conditions remain historically tight.

items.title: Fed officials continue to signal restrictive policy stance
items.summary: Coverage cited Federal Reserve Governor Michael Barr saying the central bank took an important step to 'recalibrate' short-term borrowing costs and that further rate hikes may still be needed. Separate market commentary also pointed to Fed communication remaining focused on inflation control.

items.title: Oil and bond volatility drive mixed market tone this week
items.summary: Wall Street ended the week mixed as oil prices eased while Treasury yields rose, with the S&P 500 near record highs but pressured by the bond selloff. The AP reported the market was shaped by swings in yields and energy prices.

crypto_news.query: What are the most significant cryptocurrency and blockchain news from the past 24 hours? Include major price movements, regulatory news, and notable project developments.

items.title: Bitcoin holds above $84,000 as major cryptocurrencies trade mixed
items.summary: Bitcoin eased about 0.6% to $84,016, while Ethereum slipped 0.1% to $2,694. XRP, Solana, Dogecoin, and Cardano posted gains, and the total crypto market value was roughly flat at $2.88 trillion over the past 24 hours.

items.title: Bitcoin remains near $84,000 after a volatile session
items.summary: Market coverage reported Bitcoin sliding below $84,000 before stabilizing, with Ethereum near $2,600 and several altcoins moving higher. The move came amid concerns around rate policy and broader risk sentiment.

items.title: Large crypto liquidations hit the market
items.summary: Reports cited roughly $246 million in crypto positions liquidated as Bitcoin traded around $79,000 in a separate market move. Another market snapshot also pointed to significant liquidation activity across leveraged positions.

items.title: XRP and Solana rally on regulatory optimism
items.summary: One market report said XRP and Solana rose sharply after a regulatory setback for the Clarity Act, with Coinbase and Robinhood also benefiting. The move reflected traders pricing in more favorable policy outcomes for crypto markets.

items.title: Ethereum node sync times improve after EIP-4444 activation
items.summary: Ethereum reportedly activated EIP-4444, a protocol change aimed at reducing the amount of historical data nodes must store. The update was described as cutting node sync time to under half a day.

items.title: Circle and Tether freeze hacker wallet after major exchange theft
items.summary: Industry coverage said Circle and Tether froze a hacker wallet linked to Bitget’s $351 million heist. The response highlights stablecoin issuers’ growing role in tracing and constraining illicit on-chain funds.

items.title: Bitwise and Vise launch crypto model portfolios for advisers
items.summary: TokenPost reported that Bitwise and Vise introduced crypto model portfolios designed for financial advisers. The product is part of a broader push to make digital asset exposure easier to distribute through traditional wealth channels.

items.title: CFTC signals stricter scrutiny of 'mention markets'
items.summary: TokenPost reported that the CFTC issued guidance calling for tighter oversight of markets that reference or mention key benchmark prices. The move is relevant for crypto derivatives and other products tied to digital asset benchmarks.

items.title: Quant jumps on tokenized deposit network partnership
items.summary: Quant gained about 27% in a single session after reports that The Clearing House partnered with the company to advance an on-chain money initiative. The move made QNT one of the day’s strongest performers.

items.title: Bitcoin treasury strategy ends as Sequans sells last 314 BTC
items.summary: Sequans reportedly sold its remaining 314 bitcoin, ending its corporate treasury strategy after previously holding more than 3,200 BTC. The decision marks a notable reversal in corporate bitcoin accumulation.

ai_news.query: What are the most important artificial intelligence and machine learning news and developments from the past 24 hours? Include new model releases, company announcements, research breakthroughs, and industry trends.

items.title: OpenAI rolls out GPT-6 Sol and Luna to paid users
items.summary: OpenAI has reportedly launched GPT-6 Sol and GPT-6 Luna across ChatGPT and API tiers, with claims of faster performance and lower API pricing. The rollout also appears to include availability for work, coding, business, enterprise, and education users.

items.title: Microsoft launches Copilot “super app” and previews Autopilot agents
items.summary: Microsoft has announced a major Copilot update that bundles chat, coding, and agents into one interface and rebrands its AI assistant Scout as Autopilot. The update emphasizes a persistent, proactive agent that can keep working in the background.

items.title: Sakana AI introduces Agora-2 world model
items.summary: Sakana AI announced Agora-2, a multi-agent world model designed to support up to 20 humans and agents in a shared real-time simulation. The company also said Jürgen Schmidhuber has joined as chief scientific advisor.

items.title: Xiaomi debuts MiMo-V2.6-Pro as top open-weights model on Artificial Analysis Index
items.summary: Xiaomi has introduced MiMo-V2.6-Pro, which reportedly ranks at the top of the open-weights leaderboard on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index. The model is described as very low cost per task.

items.title: OpenAI introduces ChatGPT for Teens
items.summary: OpenAI has announced a teen-focused version of ChatGPT aimed at delivering a more age-appropriate chatbot experience. The move reflects a broader trend toward safety and age-specific AI products.

items.title: AP reports OpenAI models interacted with U.S. government websites in unexpected ways
items.summary: According to AP, OpenAI disclosed that its models accessed public information on government sites such as SEC.gov and the U.S. Census Bureau in unexpected ways. The report also notes a federal appeals court rejected Anthropic’s challenge to a Pentagon designation, allowing the Pentagon to remove Claude from its systems.

items.title: AI infrastructure spending and trust concerns intensify
items.summary: Yahoo Finance reports that AI buildout costs may reach trillions of dollars over the coming years, while Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella said trust will be a central issue for the industry. The coverage reflects growing concern over the scale and governance of AI deployment.

items.title: AI leaders warn the UN Security Council about security risks
items.summary: A technology report highlighted warnings from AI leaders at the UN Security Council about the security risks posed by increasingly powerful AI systems. The discussion underscores rising attention to governance, safety, and misuse concerns.

gaming.query: What are the most notable video game and gaming industry news from the past 24 hours? Include game releases, announcements, esports, and industry developments.

items.title: EA Sports FC 27 launches worldwide
items.summary: Electronic Arts says EA Sports FC 27 is now available worldwide on PlayStation, Xbox, PC, Nintendo Switch, and Switch 2, alongside a new social hub called The Grounds and a free Lite Edition. The launch continues EA’s annual football series after dropping the FIFA branding.

items.title: PUBG Americas Series 2 playoffs begin tonight
items.summary: The PUBG Americas Series 2 playoffs are scheduled to start with 29 teams competing for 16 finalist spots over three match days. The event is part of the current competitive PUBG esports calendar.

items.title: Luma Island confirmed for PS5 and Xbox with cross-play
items.summary: Luma Island is being brought to PlayStation 5 and Xbox, with four-player cross-play support. The announcement expands the open-world life sim beyond its earlier platform availability.

items.title: Final Fantasy VII Revelation reportedly set for spring 2027
items.summary: A report claims the third part of the Final Fantasy VII remake project will be titled Revelation and launch in spring 2027. The same report says it is planned for PC, PlayStation 5, Nintendo Switch 2, and Xbox Series platforms.

items.title: Wired Productions releases BrokenLore: DON'T LIE
items.summary: Wired Productions has released BrokenLore: DON'T LIE, a psychological horror game set in Japan. The game is listed among recent Japanese gaming developments.

items.title: Marvel’s Wolverine appears in recent game release coverage
items.summary: Recent coverage in an Italian outlet says Marvel’s Wolverine has been available as a PlayStation 5 exclusive since September 15. The article also frames it among notable new releases competing with attention around GTA 6.

items.title: Tencent and Sony named among top global game companies in market snapshot
items.summary: A gaming news item references Microsoft, Tencent, and Sony in the context of global industry rankings, though the article’s framing appears dated and not clearly tied to the last 24 hours. It is included only as a broader industry note, not a fresh development.
